description: We are a team of curious, ambitious, and technology-driven individuals passionate about AI, Data Science, Space Exploration, and Scientific Research. We value creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving, and aim to turn innovative ideas into practical solutions. summary: EARTH//NEXT is a case-file investigation tool that detects trends in Earth's vegetation. Using MODIS/Terra MOD13A3.061 NDVI data from 2000–2026 via NASA AppEEARS, it compares the Nile Delta (Egypt's agricultural heartland) against the Sahara Interior (Western Desert). The Nile Delta shows a statistically significant greening trend of +0.00079 NDVI/year (p<0.001, ESI Grade A), while the Sahara shows no detectable trend (p=0.183, ESI Grade C). Every number is traceable to its source file, filter, and library version through an Evidence Receipt. The app runs fully offline from a static build — no server, no database, no runtime NASA calls. Built for the Be an Earth System Trend Detective challenge.
details:
What it does: EARTH//NEXT lets you pick a NASA Earth observation variable, compare two regions, and see whether each is trending — with full statistical transparency. Five screens walk the user through the case file: Mission Control (3D globe + featured finding), Signal Atlas (trend map), Trend Lab (answer cards + time series with CI band + evidence receipt), Compare (Region Duel side-by-side), and Crosswalk (every challenge requirement mapped to where it's answered).

How it works: A Python pipeline ingests MOD13A3.061 NetCDF files from NASA AppEEARS, applies Theil–Sen slope estimation with 95% CI, Mann–Kendall significance testing (Hamed–Rao variant for autocorrelation), and cos(latitude) area-weighted spatial means. Results are exported as JSON to web/public/data/. The Next.js frontend renders exclusively from these JSON files — static export, offline-first.

Tools used: Python 3.13 (numpy, pandas, xarray, scipy, statsmodels, pymannkendall), Next.js 14 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS, ECharts, react-globe.gl (Three.js), pydantic + Zod for dual schema validation.

Creativity: Every number shown has an Evidence Receipt — a drawer showing the exact dataset, filters applied, library versions, config hash, and data checksum that produced it. The project-defined Evidence Strength Index (ESI, 0–10) grades trend confidence from the analysis.yaml rubric. Decision Lab computes time-to-threshold and scenario fans, all labeled "Illustrative scenario — not a validated causal forecast."

Intended impact: Give students, analysts, and regional planners an honest, transparent tool that distinguishes signal from noise — and never overstates what the data can say.
